## Design

### 2026-11-08: To begin my project I had to design my robotic hand on Fusion 360. I began by trying to fit my parts into the tier 1 budget of Half Life, I achieved this by buying 3 servo motors instead of 5 which wo

**15h**

To begin my project I had to design my robotic hand on Fusion 360. I began by trying to fit my parts into the tier 1 budget of Half Life, I achieved this by buying 3 servo motors instead of 5 which would each respectively control, pinkie and index, middle and ring and thumb. The servo motors would pull on string or fishing line and an elastic cord or similar would return the finger straightened.

I took inspiration from [Shapekit](https://shapekit.cc/robot-hand?utm_source=chatgpt.com) to design my robotic hand. I built each finger myself by extruding a sketch and adding a joint to each. I reused some of the Index parts like the middle and end for other fingers as well. I made the thumb and pinkie separately as they are noticeable different in real life compared to the index, middle and ring finger.

I made many test assemblies of fingers and hands to see what worked and what didn't, The hardest part was dealing with  so many parts and not getting lost in which part goes where and how to join them. It took me an extra hour to get the palm to what I wanted. (**This accounts for one of my extra hours as I paused the lapse on accident!** ) Joinery was extremely difficult, I first began by simply using constraints for the finger joints but that made moving the finger joints unpredictable and difficult. I spent some time researching how to efficiently animate the joints and resolved that I would have to start my assembly again from scratch. Starting from scratch, I used the revolve function and limited each joint to 90 degrees to match real life movement.
